question.leadin: The Lateran Treaty governed the relationship between this country and its much larger neighbor.
question.text: Name this country, whose flag and coat of arms both depict a pair of crossed keys. Its head of state is elected through a conclave by the College of Cardinals.
question.answerHtml: Vatican City [or the Vatican City State, or Status Civitatis Vaticanae, or Stato della Città del Vaticano; prompt on the Holy See]
question.clue: Before this country was created, several men were called "prisoners" in the hill for which this country is named due to refusing to recognize authorities.

swap.text: This Ecumenical Council from 1545 to 1563 was the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant Reformation.
swap.clue: Other doctrines established by this council include the use of the deuterocanonical books in the Latin bible, as well as defining the term "transubstantiation."

question.leadin: It was defined as the official Roman Catholic Dogma in the 1854 bull Ineffabilis Deus.
question.text: Identify this concept which states that Mary, the mother of Jesus, originated free from original sin.
question.clue: That bull, Ineffabilis Deus, was issued on the day of the "Feast" of this doctrine - December 8th - by Pope Pius IV.

swap.text: Members of this organization were wounded by Ortega's government in an attack on a basilica in Diaramba. Violence against this organization prompted its leader, Pope Francis, to send Ortega a letter calling for "fraternal reconciliation."
swap.answerHtml: the Roman Catholic Church [prompt on church; prompt on clergy or priesthood]
swap.clue: One leader of this institution was critically wounded by Mehmet Ali Agca in 1981.

question.leadin: God wills this bonus! answer some of the following about the event in which other people used that motto.
question.text: The phrase Deus vult, or God Wills It, was used during by Pope Urban II during this council, which also led to the excommunication of Philip I of France. This council began a conflict led by Peter the Hermit against the Seljuk Turks.
question.clue: Due to an adulterous relationship with Bertrade de Montfort, Countess of Anjou, Philip I was excommunicated at this church council, which was preceded by the council of Placentia.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about people and things that Martin Luther didn't like.
swap.text: Luther's 95 Theses criticize the sale of these documents which offered to absolve sins of the living or dead. Johann Tetzel notably sold these documents in Germany.
swap.clue: They were first granted en-masse during the Council of Clermont for those soldiers who set out to the Levant.

question.text: Calling upon Christians to retain orthodoxy and submission to the church, Robert the Monk records that a certain pope cried this phrase at the Council of Clermont, translating to "God wills it."
question.answerHtml: Deus Vult [accept Deus lo Vult or Deus le Vult; some players may pronounce the “V” as a “W” due to classical Latin pronunciation]

swap.text: The eighth pope of this name officially recognized witches' existence with a 1484 bull. The third pope of this name excommunicated King John and convened the fourth Lateran council.
swap.clue: Yet another pope by this name issued the bull Summis Desiderantes which targeted witchcraft, and threatened to excommunicate those who read the theses of Pico della Mirandola in Rome.

question.leadin: It followed the ineffectual rule of Benedict XI.
question.text: Name this period officially lasting from 1309 to 1377 that was resolved in the Council of Constance, in which several popes generally took up residence in a certain French city.
question.clue: The man who ended this time period did so after reading a letter written by Catherine of Siena.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Great Schism of the West per part.
swap.text: At the Council of Constance, this man was elected as sole holder of the papacy, thus ending the schism.
swap.clue: This man was elected pope during the 1417 Council of Constance. The successor to Gregory XII, he ruled until 1431 when he was succeeded by Eugene IV.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about various popes.
question.text: This pope resigned in 2013, becoming the first pope since 1294 to do so.
question.answerHtml: Pope Benedict XVI [prompt on Benedict; or Joseph Aloisius Ratzinger]
question.clue: Other critics of this man attacked his lavish dress, for which he was known as "the pope of aesthetics," while others were upset by his conscription into Germany's military in World War II.

swap.text: In response to the 95 Theses, this pope issued the bull Exsurge Domine, which demanded that Luther retract a number of errors within 60 days.
swap.clue: He reaffirmed the sale of indulgences established by his predecessor, which lead to a conflict including the 95 Theses.

question.leadin: This event was caused by the election of Pope Urban VI and the accusations of intimidation which led to his election.
question.text: Name this event, during which there were two or three claimants to the Papacy, residing in Rome, France and, for a brief period, Pisa. This event is sometimes described as "great", causing confusion with a separate event of 1054.
question.answerHtml: The Western Schism [accept Great Divide or Great Occidental Schism or Schism of 1378 or Great Western Schism, do not accept or prompt on “Great Schism” or “Schism”]
question.clue: Pierre d'Ailly ("dah-YEE") and Jean Gerson ("zhawn zhair-SON") promoted a conciliar resolution to this conflict, which began when 13 rebels staged an election in Fondi ("FOHN-dee") with regalia stolen by a camerlengo.

swap.text: Clement VII was the first of two of these popes, who are not considered official by the Roman Catholic Church. Modern groups of them include the Sedevacantist ones and the Conclavist ones.
swap.clue: The last generally recognized one of these was Felix V, who reigned in the 1440s. Another one was patronized by the Crescentii and twice seized power as Boniface VII.

question.text: The appointment of the fifth and last pope of this name at the Council of Constance ended the Western Schism.
question.clue: One pope of this name, whose love for Lake Bolsena eels and Vernaccia wine was lampooned in the Divine Comedy, was a Frenchman who ordered the Aragonese crusade against Peter III for overthrowing Charles of Anjou in the Sicilian Vespers.

swap.text: The addition in question was this clause in the Nicene creed which translates to "from the Father and the Son." In greek, this clause had a literal one iota difference from the Orthodox preferred version.
swap.clue: Much of the discussion at Ferrara-Florence centered upon this Latin phrase, whose presence in the Nicene Creed was rejected by the Eastern Orthodox church. It describes the origin of the Holy Spirit.

question.text: At this event convoked in 1179 by Pope Alexander III, delegates studied the Peace of Venice, by which Frederick Barbarossa had removed his antipope, and Peter Waldo was present.

swap.leadin: This event was preceded by growing tensions between Spoletan and Roman factions over whether Arnulf or Lambert should be Holy Roman emperor.
swap.text: Name this event in which Pope Stephen VI put the rotting corpse of his predecessor, Formosus, on trial, declared Formosus's actions void, and ordered the body thrown in the Tiber.
swap.clue: Give the colloquial term for the 897 trial of Pope Formosus, in which the pontiff was charged with violating canon law by his successor and by a pissed-off Lambert II, who had previously been promised the crown.

question.leadin: Michaelist sources, such as The Chronicle of Nicholas the Minorite, were cited as proof of the intransigency of this Pope during the Apostolic Poverty Controversy. FTPE.
question.text: Name this Pope during the Avignon Papacy who succeeded Clement V in 1316. He quarreled with Emperor Louis IV of Bavaria, who under advice of William of Ockham, set up the antipope Nicholas V.

swap.leadin: In an attempt to restore his faltering reputation, this man roped Jews into participating in the rigged Disputation of Tortosa and issued a papal bull banning them from making crucifixes or binding books.
swap.text: Name this Aragonese cardinal who maintained his antipope status for a staggering twenty-eight years, because he refused to resign with his colleagues Gregory XII and John XXIII during the Council of Constance.
swap.answerHtml: Antipope Benedict XIII [or Pedro Martinez de Luna y Perez de Gotor; prompt on Benedict]
